accepts.description:
Priority-ordered list of `<provider>:<model>` bindings this agent will accept. Per project memory `project_per_worker_model_subscription`, the harness-server resolves this list against the configured AuthStore / Secrets Manager + the LLMProvider registry at spawn time and binds the agent to the first satisfiable entry. Mixed cloud+local pipelines are the natural payoff: a summarizer can lead with `local-qwen:qwen3` while a code-reviewer holds out for `anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5`.

Two equivalent shapes (per memory `project_set_scoped_accepts`):

  1. Flat array: `["anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5", "local-qwen:qwen3"]`      — single global priority list. Treated as `{default: [...]}`.

  2. Named sets: `{ default: [...], cheap: [...], frontier: [...],      bench-claude: [...], bench-gpt: [...] }` — pick one set per-job      via the `set` field on the job submission. Falls back to      `default` when the active set isn't declared on this agent.      Selecting per-job (not per-server) lets a single running harness      serve different sets concurrently — natural for benchmarking      and per-customer policy.

Validation is structural only (each leaf entry must be a non-empty `<provider>:<model>` string). Whether each entry actually exists in the registry is checked at resolve time.

Use `resolveAccepts(agent, setName)` to project to a flat list. The orchestrator does this when registering agents for a job.

adapter.description: Which adapter implementation runs this agent.

config.description: Optional adapter-specific configuration. Passed through to the adapter factory; the adapter is responsible for interpreting the shape. Use this for per-agent overrides like model name, endpoint URL (for opencode-cli with a self-hosted backend), reasoning effort, timeout, etc.

fallbackOn.description:
Per-agent runtime-fallback policy. Names of `AdapterError` subclasses (matched against `error.name`) that should trigger fall-through to the next satisfiable binding when the current binding throws.

Unset → uses the default recoverable set (BillingError, RateLimitError, NetworkError, ProviderError). AuthError + ConfigError are excluded by default because they signal structural problems (revoked key, missing model) — silent retry across providers is usually the wrong action; surface to the operator instead.

Set to `[]` to disable fallback entirely for this agent (any error is terminal, even if other accept-list entries are satisfiable).

Per slice 13c per-agent customization: catalog authors who want "never silently switch providers when an auth error occurs" default behavior get it for free; pipelines that explicitly want cross-provider auth retry opt in via `fallbackOn: [..., 'AuthError']`.

id.description: Stable id for streaming/registration. Unique within a pipeline.

skillz.description:
Skills this agent depends on. References items from the `@helmsmith/skillzkit` catalog — the procurement flow (workspace-cli) resolves each entry to markdown files + transitive dependencies and copies them into `<workspace>/.claude/{commands,skills}/` so the agent can invoke them at runtime.

skillzkit's catalog has two top-level types: SKILLs (router agents that classify natural-language requests + dispatch to commands) and Commands (everything else — slash commands, workflows, tools, integrations, atomic tasks). The categories below mirror that split plus skillzkit's sub-classification under `.claude/commands/`:

  - `routers`      — SKILL names (router agents). Lookup by name                       (e.g. `skillzkit-product-router`)   - `tools`        — local CLIs / utilities (e.g. `core:tools:npm`,                       `core:tools:gh`, `core:tools:jq`)   - `integrations` — remote services the agent connects to (e.g.                       `core:integrations:figma`, `core:integrations:linear`)   - `tasks`        — atomic action commands (smaller unit than workflow)   - `workflows`    — multi-step procedures from skillzkit's Workflow                       catalog (e.g. `engineer:feature-build`,                       `product:greenfield`)

Validation here is structural only — string non-emptiness + a closed key set. Whether each slug or skill name actually exists in the installed skillzkit catalog is checked at procure time by the workspace-cli, not at catalog parse time (so a catalog can reference skills that aren't yet installed).

Skipping this field is fine — agents without skill dependencies don't need any `.claude/` content beyond what the workspace-template ships.

systemPrompt.description: Optional system prompt; if omitted, the adapter's default applies.

ApprovalRequest.description: Payload surfaced when an Approval-tagged node pauses for review. The reviewer (or harness-server's HITL UI) inspects this, decides approve/reject, and resumes with an `ApprovalResume`.

assigneeRole.description: Org role authorized to approve (from the ApprovalTag).

attempt.description: 1-indexed attempt counter — increments each time the gate runs.

changes.description: Staged file changes the reviewer can inspect. Empty when no agent has staged changes (or no product repos are wired).

content.description: The output text the reviewer is approving — pulled from `state.output` at interrupt time.

diffSummary.description: Short human-readable summary of the staged diff (e.g. "3 files, +42 −7"), derived from `changes` at interrupt time.

kind.description: Discriminator — distinguishes approval from suspend interrupts.

nodeId.description: The original (untagged) node id whose output is being reviewed.

prUrl.description: URL of the pull request opened by an upstream `publish` node (`push-and-open-pr`), when one ran before this gate.

slaMs.description: Time-to-respond before the harness auto-rejects. harness-server arms an auto-reject timer from this value when the job pauses, re-armed across restarts from the original pause time (an SLA that expired while the server was down fires immediately).

steeringInputs.description: Optional structured input schema the reviewer fills in.

steering.description: Reviewer-provided steering text (free-form) or structured fields matching `steeringInputs`. Becomes the rejectionPayload.steering on reject; appended to `state.steering` on approve.

ApprovalTag.description: HITL gate. Pauses execution; assigns to a role; injects steering context on retry. Emits both 'sequence' (approve) and 'reject' edges.

concurrency.description: Concurrency: only 'pessimistic' (single approver locks) in v1.

steeringInputs.description: Optional structured input the reviewer fills in to steer retry.

message.description: Human-readable message embedded in the rejection payload when this assertion fails.

Catalog.description: Unified Catalog — flows + products. This is the single shape that flows through `loadCatalog: () => Promise<Catalog>`. `FlowCatalog` is the flows-only type; `Catalog` extends it with the additional axes.

products.description: Optional in v1 — workspaces without products skip this.

ChangedFile.description:
One staged change in a product repo. Populated into `state.changedFiles` before HITL interrupts; surfaced to reviewers via ApprovalRequest + the harness-server file routes.

The `id` is stable for the same `(repo, path)` within a job — UI components can use it as a React key, content-cache identifier, etc. Renames produce ONE entry with the new path + `previousPath` filled in (matches `git diff --name-status -z` rename rows).

changeKind.description: What kind of change this is. Mirrors git's name-status codes collapsed to readable form.

id.description: Stable id: `${repo}::${path}`. Suitable for URL paths after encodeURIComponent.

mimeType.description: MIME type guessed from the file extension. Hint for UI rendering; not authoritative — clients may sniff content if needed.

path.description: Path within the repo (slash-separated, no leading slash).

previousPath.description: For renames/copies, the prior path. Undefined otherwise.

repo.description: Repo name (matches an entry from `productRepos` on the JobRecord).

statusCode.description: Raw git status code (e.g., 'M', 'A', 'D', 'R100'). Preserved for clients that want git-native semantics.

CompareOp.description:
Comparison operator for `compare` expressions.

 ==, != — strict equality / inequality (===, !==); objects compare           by REFERENCE, so structurally equal objects are never ==.  <, <=, >, >= — numeric comparison; either side coerces via Number().                 NaN on either side ⇒ predicate is false.  in       — membership: rhs MUST resolve to an array; predicate is             true iff lhs (raw value) is found via Array.includes             (SameValueZero — NaN self-matches, a runtime-state-only             case since JSON cannot encode NaN). This op is             collection-only; string containment is `contains`.  contains / startsWith / endsWith — string ops: both sides must             resolve to strings, else false (no coercion, mirroring             `in`'s strictness).  matches  — regex test: both sides must resolve to strings; rhs is             compiled via `new RegExp(rhs)` (no flags) and tested             against lhs. An invalid pattern evaluates to false —             the evaluator never throws on bad data. When rhs is a             string literal, the validator additionally rejects             invalid patterns at load time.

ContextSourceDef.description:
One context-source declaration on a product. Mirrors the shape used in `<workspace>/.harness/config/context-sources.yml` and in harness-workspace.yml's per-product `contextSources` block. The loader consumes these one-per-spawned-worker when `harness context load
--product X` lands.

target.description: What to ingest: a path, an OSS package@version, or a URL.

on.description: Optional list of `NodeExit.errorName` values this edge handles (e.g. ['Timeout', 'RateLimitError', 'OutputParseError']). Omitted (or empty) → catch-all. A source node may declare any number of named error edges plus at most ONE catch-all; on an error exit the router picks the first declared edge whose `on` contains the errorName, falling back to the catch-all. Names are free-form — they match whatever the executors emit (AdapterError subclass names, 'UnknownTool', 'Timeout', …), which is runtime vocabulary the spec cannot close over.

Expression.description:
Generic expression evaluated by the runtime. Tagged-union over evaluators so we can grow the language additively.

v1 evaluator covers everything except `js`. The boolean composition primitives (`compare` / `all` / `any` / `not`) are the deliberate alternative to a JS sandbox: most catalog logic only needs simple field comparisons + AND/OR/NOT, and these primitives express that without bringing a sandbox dependency on board. The `js` kind remains in the type so authors can declare future intent, but the evaluator throws — there's no in-process JS interpreter wired.

edges.description: All edges between nodes. Routing logic lives here.

kind.description: Flow kind discriminator. Default 'work'.   - 'work' (default) — does product work; agents run for end-user value.   - 'job-definition' — emits a JobIntent (intake conversations).     Must declare `output: { kind: 'job-intent' }`.   - 'post-job' — runs after a job for cleanup/notifications.

nodes.description: All nodes (TaskSteps) in this flow. Exactly one must have `kind: 'trigger'` (the entry point).

output.description: Output contract for the terminal node. Default for `kind: 'work'` is `{ kind: 'agent-text' }`. JobDefinitionFlows MUST declare `{ kind: 'job-intent' }`.

version.description: Optional version identity (free-form, semver recommended). Gives durable checkpoints and subflow pins something stable to name; uniqueness is still keyed on `id` alone within a catalog.

FlowOutputContract.description: Output contract for a flow. Drives validator (e.g., a `kind: 'job-definition'` flow must declare `output.kind: 'job-intent'`) and JobStateMachine emission semantics (terminal node output is parsed against this shape).

FlowRunState.description: The routable run-state surface — the shape jsonpath expressions bind against at runtime. This is the data-plane half of the contract: edge conditions, gate assertions, loop paths, tool args, and node input mappings all resolve against a value of this shape. harness-core's FlowState channels must remain structurally assignable to this (compile-time-asserted there).

input.description: Job/trigger payload. Seeded once at start; never overwritten by nodes. jsonpath surface: `$.input`.

messages.description: Append-only message log (reducer-merged; safe under parallelism).

nodes.description: Per-node outputs, keyed by node id. Structured (parsed JSON) when the node declares `output.kind: 'json'`; the raw output string otherwise. jsonpath surface: `$.nodes.<id>`.

output.description: Latest text output (legacy single channel; last-write-wins). Each successful node writes here; the next node reads it as its default input. jsonpath surface: `$.output`.

approvalRequest.description: HITL payloads a reviewer UI exchanges with the runtime.

nodeExit.description: Routing exit signal + reviewer file surface.

runState.description: The run-state surface expressions bind against.

GateConfig.description: Quality gate. Runs assertions; emits 'pass' (sequence edge) or 'reject' (reject edge) based on whether all assertions hold.

JobIntent.description: The runtime representation of a JobIntent — what JobDefinitionFlows emit, what gets submitted to JobStateMachine to launch the actual work flow.

set.description: Optional: which named accepts-set to use ('default', 'cheap', 'frontier', 'bench-claude', etc.).

LoopTag.description: Iterates the same node over a collection. Composes with anything; Loop+Approval = approval per iteration; Loop+Suspend = durable iteration checkpoint.

mode.description: Sequential = one iteration at a time; parallel = N at once.

path.description: Expression resolving to the iterable. May reference flow state, product repos, prior node output, etc.

source.description: Hint about what kind of iterable `path` resolves to. The runtime uses this to pick a default collector (e.g., 'directory' walks files; 'collection' iterates an array).

MergePrConfig.description: Merge a pull request opened earlier in the same flow (by a `push-and-open-pr` node). Typically placed immediately after an `approval`-tagged node, so it only runs on the approve edge. Writes `{ mergeSha }` into `state.output` (as JSON) and onto the JobRecord (`mergeSha`). The PR to merge is read from the JobRecord's `prUrl`.

deleteBranch.description: Delete the head branch after a successful merge. Default true.

NodeExit.description: Per-node exit signal. Drives error/fallback/reject routing in the conditional-edge router. Set by every node executor; the router reads it to choose the next node id. jsonpath surface: `$.lastExit`.

NodeOutputContract.description: Per-node output contract (distinct from the flow-level FlowOutputContract, which governs the terminal node's emission). `json` makes the node's output addressable as structured data at `$.nodes.<id>` — the enabling contract for gates and conditional edges over agent results. `schema` is declared-but-not-enforced (reported via onUnsupported as 'node-output-schema').

ProductDef.description: Product = a tenant boundary with its declared content sources. Per project_authority_model_jobs_pipelines, products are admin-owned shapes the runtime references at job-acceptance time. They live alongside pipelines in the unified Catalog.

repos.description:
Per-product git repos. When present, harness-server can resolve `repos` for the container path (slice 9d-4) without the job submission having to carry them — caller submits productId, the server looks up the repo list. Per memory `project_authority_model_jobs_pipelines`: products are admin- owned, so this is the authoritative source of truth for which repos belong to a product.

When absent, callers must pass `repos` on the submission body (slice 9d-4 fallback path).

ProductRepo.description:
One product repo declaration — name + git clone URL + optional baseRef + optional in-container mount path. Used by spawn-worker (slice 9d) to pre-clone the repo as a bare and add a per-job worktree before the devcontainer boots.

Shape mirrors `SpawnRepoSpec` from `@helmsmith/harness-server` (which the spawn primitive owns) — declared here so the catalog can carry the same shape without harness-core having to depend on harness-server. Values cross the package boundary structurally.

baseRef.description: Optional base ref to clone (default: remote's default branch).

cloneUrl.description: git clone URL — SSH (`git@github.com:org/repo.git`) or HTTPS (`https://github.com/org/repo.git`). For private repos under HTTPS, callers can inject a PAT via `cloneEnv` on the worker spawn (slice 9d-2-creds) or use the URL form `https://<token>@github.com/...`.

name.description: Local name — also the directory under `/workspace/<name>/` in the container's synthetic monorepo (PRD F19).

path.description: Optional in-container mount path. Defaults to `/workspace/<name>/` per F19's synthetic-monorepo convention.

PublishConfig.description:
Delivery of the flow's output to an external destination. The `publish-*` family — `push-and-open-pr`, `merge-pr`, and (future) `upload-to-s3`, `export-to-figma`, … — keeps the "how the work ships" decision in the authored flow graph rather than baked into the orchestrator. The runtime executor (`publish-executor.ts`) reads `action` to pick the path.

GitHub credentials for the `*-pr` actions resolve through a cascade (local `gh` → controlplane-issued App token); the executor takes a `GitHubCredentialResolver` from `RunJobDeps.githubResolver`.

PushAndOpenPrConfig.description: Push the per-job branch to `origin` and open a pull request. Placed after an agent has staged + committed changes in the worktree. Writes `{ prUrl, prNumber, branchName }` into `state.output` (as JSON) and onto the JobRecord (`branchName`, `prUrl`).

base.description: Base branch the PR targets. Default: the repo's default branch (resolved via the GitHub API).

body.description: PR body (Markdown). Defaults to a generated body referencing the job and its base ref.

draft.description: Open as a draft PR. Default false.

repo.description: Which product repo to push — must match a name in `JobRecord.productRepos`. Omittable when the product has exactly one repo.

title.description: PR title. Defaults to a generated title from the job name/id.

RejectEdge.description: Emitted only by Approval-tagged nodes and `kind: 'gate'` nodes when they reject. Carries a structured rejection payload (steering context, findings, attempt counter). The reject edge is the only edge that may form a cycle (retry-with-context loops).

onMaxAttempts.description: Where to go when maxAttempts is exceeded. Default: fail the flow.

RejectionPayload.description: The runtime payload carried by reject edges. Becomes input context to the destination node.

maxAttempts.description: TOTAL attempts including the first (1 ≡ no retry). Retries fire only on error exits — reject exits are authored flow control.

ScriptConfig.description: Code execution. The script's source body is dropped to a temp file and run via the language's interpreter; state.output is piped to the script as stdin (UTF-8 string), and the script's stdout becomes the new state.output. A curated FlowRunState view (incl. `input`, excl. `nodes`/`messages`/`changedFiles` for env-size reasons) is exposed as JSON via the `HARNESS_STATE_JSON` environment variable — scripts needing a node's output should declare an `input` mapping, which arrives on stdin. Non-zero exit routes to the node's error edge.

secrets.description: Credential references resolved through the CredentialBroker at dispatch time and injected as environment variables — the same auth surface tools use, so secrets never appear literally in catalogs. Keys are env var names; resolved values win over any same-named `env` entry.

timeoutMs.description: Hard timeout for the script run. Default 30s. SIGTERM on expiry, SIGKILL after a short grace period if the child ignores SIGTERM.

SubflowConfig.description: Invoke another flow as a sub-flow. The parent pauses until the sub-flow terminates; sub-flow output flows in as this node's output.

version.description: Optional version pin against the target flow's `version`. Recorded but not enforced yet — subflows resolve by flowId in the loaded catalog (reported via onUnsupported as 'subflow-version-pin').

SuspendRequest.description: Payload surfaced when a Suspend-tagged node pauses. The caller is responsible for scheduling the resume — timer-based or event-based. The resume value is unused (suspend has no decision; resume is the "wake up" signal itself).

changes.description: Staged file changes pending review while the job is suspended.

SuspendTag.description: Durable execution checkpoint. Serializes state, kills the worker, hydrates a new worker on timer expiration or external signal.

TaskStep.description: The single canvas primitive — every node on the flow graph is a TaskStep. Polymorphic via the `kind` discriminator; per-kind config goes in `config`, tags add behavioral modifiers, policy controls reliability, joinStrategy defines how multiple incoming edges combine.

config.description: Per-kind config (typed by which kind is set).

effect.description: Side-effect classification. Declarative for now (reported via onUnsupported): the runtime does not yet consult it when deciding whether a node is safe to re-run on replay/retry. Publish-family nodes are inherently 'side-effecting'.

id.description: Stable id; referenced by edges. Unique within a flow.

input.description:
Input mapping — how this node composes its effective input from run state, instead of implicitly consuming the previous node's `output` string. Two forms:

  - A single Expression: resolves to the effective input. Strings     pass through raw; other values are JSON-serialized.   - A Record mapping name → Expression: each field resolves against     state and the whole object is JSON-serialized. This is how a     node consumes MORE than one upstream value: `$.input`,     `$.nodes.<id>`, `$.rejectionPayload`, …

The single-Expression form is detected by a string `kind` field, so mapping keys must not be named `kind`.

Omitted → legacy behavior: the node reads `state.output` as-is.

joinStrategy.description: Barrier over this node's forward-edge (sequence/conditional) sources: 'all' waits for every source, 'any' fires on the first arrival, nOfM on the nth — exactly once per run. Only applies when EXPLICITLY declared: an undeclared multi-in node runs once per arriving branch (no implicit join — an implicit 'all' would deadlock diamonds whose branches route conditionally). Join nodes may not be targeted by error/fallback/reject edges (validator- rejected); joins inside reject cycles are unsupported.

output.description: Per-node output contract. `json` → the runtime parses the node's output into `state.nodes[id]` (parse failure exits with errorName 'OutputParseError', routable via an error edge). Omitted / `text` → `state.nodes[id]` holds the raw output string.

tags.description: Behavioral modifier tags. Multiple allowed; render order is Loop top-left, Approval/Suspend top-right. Approval and Suspend are mutually exclusive on the same node.

terminal.description: Set on nodes with no outgoing edges. Defaults to 'success'.

onError.description: Behavior when an unhandled error occurs:  - 'propagate' (default) — fail the flow  - 'continue' — log and proceed past this node  - 'fallback' — route to the node's fallback edge if present

ToolConfig.description:
Deterministic tool/API call. References a tool by id (resolved against the tool catalog or skillzkit). The `args` map is merged with the ToolDef's own argument template at dispatch time; values may be Expressions (jsonpath/literal) for state-driven argument synthesis, same evaluator the conditional-edge router uses.

Example flow-side reference:     { id: "lint", kind: "tool", config: {         toolId: "core:tools:eslint",         args: { path: { kind: "jsonpath", path: "$.output" } } } }

TransformConfig.description: Pure data shaping. Evaluates an expression against current flow state.

TriggerConfig.description: Entry point. Exactly one trigger node per flow.
